quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The paper is a relevant core MBSE/CubeSat verification case with clear mission context, tool/method identification, and model-linked verification claims. Its main weaknesses are the narrow communications-only scope, absence of EPS content, limited reproducibility assets, and largely unquantified outcome evidence.

RQ1.rationale: The study describes a general SysML/OOSEM nanosatellite system-modeling architecture and communications verification workflow, but it does not address EPS and relies on existing requirements/design/test documents rather than minimal behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: It claims model reliability checking, traceability, reuse, automated compliance updates, and reduced reporting time at CubeSat system/subsystem level, but not EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, or integrability outcomes.

RQ3.rationale: Verification procedures are integrated into SysML models for the communications subsystem using test-plan-derived verification models and external test setup integration; no EPS model or EPS pre-physical verification is reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The supplied corpus metadata shows retrieval through multiple Scopus query routes and semantic-scholar title enrichment. No previous extraction, sources.bib, or other papers were used.

RQ1: The study provides a general EIRSAT-1 CubeSat system-modeling architecture using SysML, CATIA Magic, and OOSEM, organized into reusable project packages.
Modeling is not based on minimal prior behavioral knowledge; it depends on existing requirements, design documents, test documents, communication components, and traditional end-to-end test plans.
The exemplar is communications subsystem verification, not EPS, so transfer to EPS is only indirect.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include full requirements traceability, model-flow reliability assessment, automatic requirements-table updates, reduced documentation/reporting effort, and reuse in similar verification scenarios.
Outcome evidence is mostly qualitative and case-workflow based; only automatic update and integration with the actual test setup are directly reported, with no metrics or baseline comparison.
No EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, integrability, or flight/operational outcomes are reported.
RQ3: Verification procedures are integrated into the model by creating CATIA Magic verification models from traditional end-to-end test plans.
The communications model exchanges parameters with a Python client and ground-station test setup, while parametric diagrams validate data and update requirements compliance artifacts.
This is model-integrated communications verification during Phase C-D, not EPS verification and not clearly prior to all physical development.
